votes.evidence:
Traced the path from the TaskRun post_save receiver to the Celery task in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215.

- receivers.py:125-138 registers `_start_stamphog_review` via `transaction.on_commit`; receivers.py:210-236 wraps `queue_inbox_pr_review` in a bare `except Exception` and calls `logger.exception("review_hog_stamphog_inbox_review_queue_failed")`. So the premise "the enqueue exception is swallowed after commit" is correct as far as it goes, but the failure is logged with a traceback, not silent.
- The swallow is the explicitly stated contract of this hook, not an oversight: receivers.py:213 docstring "Fire-and-forget the hosted Stamphog review; the broker being down must never surface into the saver", and it mirrors the pre-existing sibling leg `_start_review` at receivers.py:246 ("Temporal being down must never surface into the saver"). Both are pinned by tests: products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:302-313 (temporal down) and :358-370 (broker down, "Same contract as the ReviewHog leg").
- The receiver runs inside tasks' save path (receivers.py:79-84 docstring; handle_task_run_saved is exception-proof end to end), so a durable outbox row "in the same transaction" as the suggestion proposes would have to be written from a foreign product's post_save on a hot model, the exact coupling this module's design avoids.
- Celery already retries the publish: installed celery 5.6.3 has `task_publish_retry=True` with policy `{max_retries: 3, interval_start: 0, interval_max: 1, interval_step: 0.2}` by default and nothing in posthog/settings/celery.py overrides it, so `.delay()` only raises after a broker outage longer than the built-in retry window.
- Recovery paths the finding says do not exist do exist, partially: (a) the receiver deliberately re-fires on every later TaskRun output save carrying `pr_url` (receivers.py:79-84; tasks.py:1120-1124 "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL"), and on the tasks architecture the run stays `in_progress` with a PR follow-up loop babysitting it (receivers.py:5-8), so later output writes are the norm, not the exception; (b) every later head-changing push re-reviews through the webhook carve-out (tasks.py:143-166, 865-880), which is not blocked by bot/draft status.
- What remains: a Redis outage that outlass Celery's publish retry, coinciding with the single `pr_url` save, followed by no further output save and no further push on that PR. The initial draft-time verdict for that one PR is then not produced until the next PR event. That is the residual, but it is the documented accepted contract of both legs, and Redis being down for seconds also breaks the Django cache and every other Celery dispatch in the process, so an outbox-plus-dispatcher for this hook alone is out of proportion to the trigger.
votes.refutation: The finding treats the swallow as a bug, but the code declares it as the contract (receivers.py:213, :246), tests enforce it for both the Temporal and the broker leg (test_inbox_trigger.py:302-313, :358-370), and the claim that nothing can recover the review is contradicted by the receiver's deliberate re-fire on later output saves (tasks.py:1120-1124) and the webhook carve-out on later pushes (tasks.py:143-166). Celery's default publish retry (3 attempts, sub-second) already covers transient broker blips. The only unrecovered case is a multi-second broker outage at the exact moment of the one pr_url save with no subsequent PR activity, and the proposed fix (an outbox table written from a cross-product post_save on a hot model plus a retrying dispatcher) is a design change disproportionate to that trigger. This is a design preference against a documented, tested, precedent-matching choice, not a defect.

votes.refutation: The finding's factual chain holds (a failed `.delay()` after commit is only logged, and the webhook carve-out covers only later head-changing events), but it does not identify a defect against the code's contract. The leg is documented and unit-tested as fire-and-forget with a log line, mirrors the ReviewHog Temporal leg in the same module, and is no less durable than the webhook view's own bare `.delay()` (which 500s with no GitHub redelivery). The loss window is a broker outage coinciding with the one output save that first carries `pr_url`, on a PR that then never receives another push and whose run never writes output again; a broker outage of that kind already drops all Stamphog webhook deliveries and most of the platform's Celery work. The suggested fix (outbox table plus retrying dispatcher) is a heavyweight architectural addition for a rare, platform-wide failure mode with existing partial recovery (later pushes via the carve-out, later output saves via the receiver). This is a design preference about durability level, not a must/should-fix bug.

votes.evidence:
Worktree: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215 (PR #75215 touches products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py and products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py, so the code is in scope).

Trigger in production: `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:149) calls `process_inbox_pr_review.delay(...)`. The broker is Redis (`CELERY_BROKER_URL = REDIS_URL`, posthog/settings/celery.py:26). Installed Celery 5.6.3 defaults: `task_publish_retry=True`, policy `{max_retries: 3, interval_start: 0, interval_step: 0.2, interval_max: 1}` (verified by importing celery.app.defaults in the flox venv; no override anywhere in posthog/ or products/). So `.delay()` already retries the publish on connection errors; the exception only escapes when Redis is unreachable for longer than ~0.6-1s at the exact instant the TaskRun output commit fires the `on_commit` hook. That is the entire reachable window per PR.

What happens then: `_start_stamphog_review` (receivers.py:232-236) does `logger.exception("review_hog_stamphog_inbox_review_queue_failed")` - not silent; it surfaces in logs/error tracking.

Recovery paths the finding says do not exist:
1. Receiver re-fire: `handle_task_run_saved` re-fires on every TaskRun save whose `update_fields` includes `output` or is None (receivers.py:79-83), and the queued task is explicitly designed for that: "The receiver re-fires on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL, so dedupe keys on the PR's CURRENT head" (tasks.py:1124-1128). Any later output save (agent server syncs, `pr_merged` backstop write at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:229-236 via `_record_run_output_field` which saves `update_fields=["output","updated_at"]` at line 292) re-queues the review.
2. Webhook carve-out: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (tasks.py:143-215) reviews bot-authored draft self-driving PRs on synchronize/reopen/base-retarget. It resolves the run via `find_signal_implementation_run` (tasks.py:190-195) and the acting-reviewer hook (tasks.py:201-205); it does NOT require a prior inbox ReviewRun to exist. So the first push after the lost queue produces a full StampHog review of the PR. The finding's premise that the webhook path "cannot recover" is only true for a draft PR that never receives another push and whose run output is never saved again.

Precedent/contract: the sibling ReviewHog leg `_start_review` (receivers.py:271-273) has the identical fire-and-forget contract for Temporal being down, and the PR's own test `test_stamphog_queue_failure_never_raises_into_the_save_path` (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:358-368) codifies "the Celery broker being down must cost a log line". Redis being down for seconds also degrades the rest of the app (cache, flags, sessions) in the same request, so the outage is not a stamphog-specific failure that an outbox table would isolate.
votes.refutation: The described trigger (Redis unreachable beyond Celery's built-in 3-attempt publish retry, exactly at the on_commit instant of one TaskRun output save) is reachable in production only as a narrow coincidence, and when it happens the loss is logged with a traceback, is recovered by the next output save (the queued task is designed to dedupe on re-fires) and by the next push via the webhook carve-out (which needs no prior run). The claim that the review is "silently" and "permanently" lost with no recovery path is contradicted by receivers.py:232-236, tasks.py:1124-1128 and tasks.py:143-215. Requiring an outbox table plus a retrying dispatcher for this window is an architectural preference that also contradicts the module's stated contract (identical to the pre-existing ReviewHog leg and asserted by the PR's test). Not a should_fix defect; at most a design note, so is_real=false.
